tools.name: start_load_test
tools.description: Load tests the user's app on a real cloud server and returns a run id. The target is a public or connected GitHub repository URL, or a Docker image. Lite is free once per person (500 users, 4 minutes). Standard (2,500 users, 10 minutes) costs 1 credit and Massive (10,000 users, 15 minutes) costs 3.

tools.name: get_test_status
tools.description: Where a run stands: building, starting servers, running (with live users, requests per second, p95 latency and error rate) or finished.

tools.name: get_test_report
tools.description: The full report of a finished run: the verdict, users held, requests per second, p95 latency and errors at each load level, what ran out first, CPU, busiest thread and memory on the server and per service, connections to the database and other dependencies, what the responses were, and which server

tools.name: get_test_timeline
tools.description: How a run moved over time: users, requests per second, p95 latency and error rate, averaged into a fixed number of points. Works while a run is going and after it ends.

tools.name: list_load_tests
tools.description: The account's runs, newest first: id, status, size, target, requests, when it ran and why it failed if it did.

tools.name: stop_load_test
tools.description: Stops a run that is waiting or running and deletes its servers. A run stopped before its servers were up uses no credit. A run stopped while the load is going is not refunded, and its report covers what was measured until then. Ask the user first.

tools.name: delete_load_test
tools.description: Deletes a run and its report and measurements for good. A running run has to be stopped first. Ask the user first.

tools.name: set_current_server
tools.description: Tells a run which server the user already hosts the app on, so the report says whether that server is enough, how close to the limit it would be and what to change. Or set recommend to true to go back to a recommended size. The report is recomputed from the stored measurements, no new run needed.

tools.name: send_feedback
tools.description: Tells Stresix whether a finished run's report was useful, with an optional note. Only send what the user actually said. Sending again replaces the earlier answer.

tools.name: inspect_target
tools.description: Reads a repository before testing it: the port it listens on, the environment variables the code reads, the framework, whether it needs a database, and its branches. For a Docker image it only checks the reference. Use it before start_load_test.

tools.name: list_github_repos
tools.description: The GitHub repositories the user gave Stresix access to, including private ones. Public repositories work without connecting GitHub.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: The account's credits, whether the free Lite run is still available, whether GitHub is connected, what each run size costs and the credit packs on sale.

tools.name: buy_credits
tools.description: Makes a checkout link for a credit pack: Starter is 5 credits for $10, Pro is 25 credits for $40. Nothing is charged by this tool. The user opens the link and pays in their browser, and the credits arrive a minute later. Only call it when the user asked to buy credits.

tools.name: redeem_code
tools.description: Adds the credits of a promo code to the account. Only use a code the user gave you.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "inspect_target" references sensitive artifacts (environment variable). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: start_load_test, get_test_report · Private data: get_test_report, inspect_target, list_github_repos · Public sink: send_feedback · Destructive: start_load_test, get_test_status, get_test_report, get_test_timeline, stop_load_test, delete_load_test, set_current_server, send_feedback, get_account.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: start_load_test, get_test_report · Private data: get_test_report, inspect_target, list_github_repos · Public sink: send_feedback · Destructive: start_load_test, get_test_status, get_test_report, get_test_timeline, stop_load_test, delete_load_test, set_current_server, send_feedback, get_account

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
